mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals the start of a monetary easing cycle, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction, reducing equity risk appetite and compressing forward discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rate hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, which reduces unemployment risk and increases equity risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong employment periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below 100,000 jobs triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing forward discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in weak employment periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) above 98.5 signals a supply-side expansion, reducing near-term demand pressures and compressing forward discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in high-supply periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) above 590 signals stronger near-term demand, which reduces discounting of expected cash flows and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in high-demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in retail sales (HOUST) below 500 triggers a risk-off reaction, compressing forward discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in low-demand periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index over 3 consecutive months signals disinflation, lowering real discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in disinflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
